memory_candidates.content: task-lock.sh defines GATE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS (default 600000) inside its own process, invoked as a separate `bash task-lock.sh ...` subprocess from verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run(). That default never leaks back into the calling verify-deploy.sh process's own environment. Any new logic in verify-deploy.sh that needs to reason about that budget (e.g. computing a fraction of it for a contention threshold) must re-declare the SAME default inline (`${GATE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_BUDGET_MS:-600000}`) rather than reading the bare variable, or the computed threshold silently becomes 0. Caught by an isolated logic-only smoke test before running the real fixture suite.

Joining a bash array with a multi-character separator via `IFS=', '; echo "${arr[*]}"` silently collapses to only the FIRST character of IFS (',' here), losing the space -- a real, easy-to-miss bug caught only by actually printing the joined result. The correct idiom for a multi-character join is `printf '%s, ' "${arr[@]}" | sed 's/, $//'` (or equivalent trailing-strip), never the IFS/`[*]` expansion when the separator is more than one character.

generate-context-line-counts.sh and check-extension-docs.sh both refuse to run from the agent-system source-store scripts/ directory by default (their deploy-root-guard assumes a deployed .claude/scripts/ tree), but both honor a documented bypass: `REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/<script>.sh`. Needed whenever a source-store edit's Rule-R-exact line_count must be regenerated before redeploying.
